verdict.rationale: Zapier's core Zap workflows are event-triggered automations. Community users describe them as "if this then that" workflows with multiple IFs and THENs, and the docs reference Zap workflows and polling/webhook triggers. However, the first-party evidence for user-defined rules is thin; the trigger mechanics are documented mainly for integration builders, and users report that conditional-logic escape hatches are limited. missing for 10: first-party docs describing how users define trigger→action rules with conditions and filters, evidence of richer conditional/branching rule logic (community reports gaps here), documentation of AI-native rule authoring in plain language.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Zapier allows more simultaneous IFs & THENs
simple 'if this then that' types of workflows
Zap workflows can connect with 9,000+ apps
webhooks, polling triggers, and HTTP middleware
